Post 1
ASX 200 closed July at 8,967.70, up 2.15% for the month but still 2.56% off its 52-week high. A solid run, though Thursday's 70.90-point drop reminded bulls the ceiling is still in play. #ASX #ausbiz

Post 2
🔺 Energy led all sectors in July, surging 11.80%. Financials added 6.23%. On the other end, IT fell 3.34% and Materials dropped 2.25%, keeping the month's gains narrowly concentrated. #ASX #energy #ausbiz

Post 3
📉 Liontown fell 10.86% and Champion Iron dropped 8.82% on the final session alone — the worst prints in the ASX 200. Materials weakness was not evenly spread; lithium and iron ore names bore the brunt. #ASX #mining #ironore

Post 4
🛢️ Energy's 11.80% monthly surge was the dominant sector story of July, outpacing every other group by at least 5.57 percentage points and dragging broader index gains despite Materials and IT headwinds. #ASX #energy #ausbiz

Post 5
ASX 200 sits 2.56% below its 52-week high with the 9,000-point level unbroken. Energy at +11.80% could extend or mean-revert hard. Does the index clear 9,000 in August, or does Materials drag it lower? Reply with your call. #ASX #ausbiz

Post 1

Health Care bled 1.84% while Materials surged 1.42% — the ASX 200 barely moved, closing +9.10pts at 8,976.80. Two sectors pulling in opposite directions, a 0.10% net result. 2.46% from a 52-week high. #ASX #ausbiz

Post 2

📈 Materials +1.42% led Friday's winners. 🔻 Health Care -1.84% was the session's drag, with CSL down 3.81%. Consumer Staples fell 1.26%. The rotation story is real — defensives sold, cyclicals bought. #ASX #mining #healthcare

Post 3

MP1 closed at AUD 18.10, up 11.52% — Megaport's move was the session's sharpest large-cap tech print. WiseTech fell 4.20% on the same day. Tech gave with one hand, took with the other. #ASX #ausbiz #tech

Post 4

🪙 Gold at AUD 5,793.03/oz with AUD/USD at 0.7021. Silver AUD 83.28/oz. A firm local gold price underpinned Materials sector strength today. Platinum AUD 2,407.78/oz. #ASX #gold #metals #mining

Post 5

ASX sits 2.46% off its 52-week high after a 2.33% weekly gain. The question now: can Materials hold the lead into next week, or does Health Care's selloff deepen? Where do you see the index by Friday? #ASX #ausbiz #investing
